# v3.22

Rolls up the six dev pre-releases since v3.16 — **v3.17-dev** through
**v3.22-dev**.

The headline is that **every report and dashboard in the app now remembers the
view you set up**. Alongside that, one long-standing import message that said
something untrue has been corrected.

## Fixed — pages remember your view

Until now, a page that held a view you had built up — filters, search, sort,
grouping, geography scope, a projection horizon, which page of results you were
on — would throw it away the moment you left. Open someone's record from a list,
press Back, and you were returned to the defaults with the whole view to rebuild.
For anything involving checking several people in turn, that meant re-picking the
scope every single time.

All of these now keep the view in the page address and restore it on the way
back:

- **Compliance Planning** — the scope, the programs and targets you picked, and
  the renewal window. This was the one originally reported: clicking a name in
  **Renewals at risk** and pressing Back emptied the planner.
- **Program dashboards** — the **View** scope and the **Compliance as of**
  horizon.
- **Offering dashboards** — the country/region selector, which previously reset
  to empty and showed nothing at all.
- **Dashboard** — the geography scope and the "include expired" tickbox.
- **Theatre/Region/Country Comparison** — the largest of them: geography mode,
  date range (including a custom one), the function, product and type filters,
  the comparison mode and the column sort.
- **Training Catalogue Health** — the product, type and status filters, plus the
  column sort.
- **Program Compliance Trend** — the selected program and the
  theatre/region/country scope, plus the column sort.
- **Renewal Forecast** — the product filter and the theatre/region/country
  scope, plus the column sort.

Nothing to turn on. Open a record, press Back, and the view is as you left it.

**A useful side effect: these pages are now bookmarkable and shareable.** Set a
report up the way you want it, copy the address, and whoever opens it sees the
same view — same filters, same scope, same sort.

**Old or stale links stay safe.** A link naming something that is no longer there
— a filter for a deleted product, a sort on a column that has gone, a scope a
program no longer offers — falls back to the default view rather than showing you
an empty table or an unsorted one.

## Fixed — the import summary no longer claims ambiguity it never saw

Importing an Excel file whose Completed Date column holds real Excel date cells
always ended with this line in the Issues panel:

> All dates fit both DD/MM/YYYY and MM/DD/YYYY — parsed as DD/MM/YYYY (the
> system default).

It was untrue, and it appeared even for files full of dates that can only be
month-first. **Your dates were always imported correctly** — this was a wrong
message, not wrong data. Cells Excel stores as real dates are read by their true
underlying value, so the format detector skips them; it simply never lowered its
opening assumption that both formats fitted when there was nothing to check.

The detector now reports only what it actually read:

- An Excel file whose dates are real date cells says **nothing** about date
  formats — no ambiguity warning, and no "Dates parsed as…" line either, because
  no format was ever applied. One fewer entry in the Issues count.
- A file that genuinely can't be disambiguated still gets the same warning it
  always did.
- A file mixing the two now says how many cells the warning is about, rather than
  speaking for the whole column.

The "This file looks like MM/DD/YYYY" prompt, the mixed-format rejection and the
day/month-swap correction are all unchanged.

## Changed — restoring the view is now enforced by the build

The three pages fixed first were each the same mistake, and each was found only
because someone hit it: restoring the view was a written convention, and a
convention holds until the next person writes a page.

The build now checks every page that holds a view and refuses a new one that
cannot restore it. Turning the check on surfaced five existing pages with the
same problem; all five are the later entries in the list above, so that backlog
is closed and the list is empty. A new report inherits the rule automatically
rather than depending on whoever writes it remembering.

## Also in this release

- Development sessions for this repository now start from the current code
  automatically, and report the version they are working from. This affects only
  how the project is developed; it changes nothing about the application.

## Upgrading

**No database changes and no configuration changes.** Existing bookmarks keep
working exactly as before — they simply open at the default view, as they always
did.
